generic: They say the road out east has been quiet for weeks. Too quiet for anyone's liking.
Prices went up again. Nobody will say who decided that.
Somebody saw lights over the water three nights running.
The wells have tasted of iron since the spring. Ask anyone.
There is work going at the old yard, but nobody comes back talking about it.
A stranger passed through last week and paid in coins nobody recognised.
Half the town swears the bells rang at the wrong hour.
The guards changed their patrol. That never happens for nothing.
Word is a whole caravan turned back before it reached the pass.
Something got into the storehouse. They are calling it dogs.

nervous: I should not be saying this, but people have been going missing off the north road. Please do not repeat it.
You did not hear it from me. Something is wrong at the water works and nobody will admit it.
Every night this week I have heard someone moving outside. Every night. I have stopped opening the shutters.
calm: There is talk of trouble at the border. I would not act on it yet.
People are saying the harvest will fail. People say that most years.
A rumour is going around about the magistrate. I will wait until somebody puts a name to it.
aggressive: Somebody has been skimming the shipments, and when I find out who, they will be missing teeth.
Ask the pack at the tavern about the fight last week. Ask them who started it. They will lie.
There is a crew working this district that thinks nobody is watching. Somebody is.
melancholic: The old family on the hill left in the night. Nobody has said why, and nobody will.
They say the river took another one last month. It always takes somebody.
This place used to be full. Now the rumours are all we have left to pass around.
sanguine: Have you heard? There is going to be a festival, and the whole street is already arguing about the music.
Word is somebody came into money and is being very quiet about it. Wonderful, isn't it?
Everyone is talking about the new arrival. I intend to find out everything before the week is out.
cautious: I have heard the same story from three people, which is exactly why I do not trust it.
There is supposed to be easy work down at the docks. Easy work usually costs something.
Check who holds the debt before you believe anything about that shop closing.
impulsive: They say the vault under the mill is still full. I nearly went last night.
There is a fight on at the yard right now, apparently. Come on.
Somebody left a whole cart unattended by the gate. A whole cart. Unattended.
stoic: Talk says the winter will be hard. It usually is.
Two men vanished off the pass road. That is what the road does.
The prices climbed again. Complaining has never brought one of them down.
paranoid: Count the guards on the east gate. Then count them tomorrow. You will see.
The letters are being opened. I do not care who says otherwise, I have seen the seals.
Whoever is asking questions about the old warehouse is not asking for themselves.
empathetic: The family on the corner lost everything and the whole street is pretending not to notice.
They say the innkeeper's boy has not been the same since the spring. I believe it.
There is gossip going round about her, and I wish people could hear themselves.
authoritative: The shipment records do not add up, and I intend to have an answer by the week's end.
There is talk of a strike at the yard. It will be settled properly or it will be settled by me.
Somebody is giving orders in this district who has no standing to give them.
scholarly: Three separate accounts describe the same lights over the marsh, and none of them agree on the colour.
The archive lost a whole year of records to a fire that nobody recorded.
There is a manuscript circulating that claims the city is older than its charter. Poorly sourced, but interesting.
artistic: The bells rang wrong on Tuesday and nobody else seems to have heard it. I have not stopped thinking about it.
They say the painter on the square stopped taking work. I know why. I would have stopped too.
Something in this town has changed colour this season. I cannot name it, but it has.
adventurous: There is a pass nobody has walked in ten years, and I have found somebody who says it is open again.
The maps are wrong about the north ridge. I intend to prove it.
They say a ship came in with a hold full of things without names. I want to see it.
nurturing: Those children have been sleeping in the yard again. Somebody ought to do something, so I will.
They say the old woman on the lane has not opened her door in days. I am going round with soup.
There is sickness on the south side. Keep your people home if you can.
mischievous: You want to know who the constable's wife has been visiting? Buy me a drink.
Somebody swapped the ledgers at the customs house. I would never say who.
There is a rumour going round that I started, and it has come back to me improved.
cynical: They say the new tax pays for the roads. Look at the roads.
Somebody will be blamed for the missing grain. It will not be whoever took it.
Every rumour in this town is a bill somebody is trying not to pay.
disciplined: The night watch has been three men short for a month. It is in the roster, if anybody bothered to read it.
Stores went out unlogged twice this week. That is how a place starts to rot.
There is talk about the new officer. I will judge them on their drills, not on gossip.
fatalistic: They say the mine will reopen. It will flood again, the same as before.
Whatever is coming up the road is already on its way. Talking about it changes nothing.
The signs are all there. They were there last time too, and nobody moved.
grumpy: Everyone is repeating the same nonsense about the bridge and not one of them has walked it.
They put a new stall on the square. Ruined the square.
Somebody's dog got into the stores. I said this would happen. Nobody listened.
loyal: People are saying things about my employer that they would not say to his face, and they had better not.
There is a rumour about the guard captain. I served under her. It is a lie.
Whatever you have heard about that family, they stood by this town when nobody else did.
brave: They say something is living in the drains under the market. I am going down there tomorrow.
Half the street will not walk past the old house after dark. I walk past it every night.
There is talk of bandits on the east road. Let them come this way.
timid: I heard something about the tower, but please do not ask me to repeat it.
People are talking, and I would rather not be seen talking with them.
There is a man asking about strangers. I did not tell him anything. I promise.
hedonistic: The cellar at the inn has something new in it, and the innkeeper is pretending it does not exist.
They say there is a party at the big house that nobody is invited to. Nobody stays uninvited for long.
Word is the new place on the square pours honestly. That is worth more than any secret.
apathetic: Something happened at the docks. People are upset about it.
They say the council is falling apart. I suppose it might be.
There is a rumour going round. I have not bothered to learn which one.
